claim_text: 來源機構：Journal of Computer Assisted Learning (Wiley)；資料標題：From Design to Classroom Adoption: Teachers' Perspectives on AI‐powered Writing Analytics in Resource‐Constrained Contexts；來源刊登日：2026-10-30。作者摘要報告：研究從教師觀點系統評估一款 AIED-Unplugged 學習分析工具的易用性、接受度與教學相關性，以支援資源受限情境的寫作實踐且不加深數位不平等；採混合方法，巴西公私立高中 9 名教師依預設情境以放聲思考程序使用該應用程式，再填寫科技接受模式（TAM）與系統易用性量表（SUS）並受半結構訪談；作者報告量表顯示接受度與易用性高，教師認為工具有用、易於整合。（AI 輔助摘要，未經真人逐則審稿；請參閱原文。）
source_title: From Design to Classroom Adoption: Teachers' Perspectives on AI‐powered Writing Analytics in Resource‐Constrained Contexts

original_excerpt: This study aims to systematically evaluate the usability, acceptability and pedagogical relevance of an AIED-Unplugged learning analytics tool from teachers' perspectives, in order to guide the development of user-centered design strategies and support writing practices in resource-constrained educational settings without deepening digital inequities. … We employed a mixed-methods approach involving nine teachers, who downloaded an AIED-U application and followed a predefined usage scenario according to a think-aloud protocol. … Afterwards, participants filled out the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and System Usability Scale (SUS) questionnaires, taking part in a moderated semi-structured interview guided by an interview script. … The quantitative findings indicated high levels of acceptance and usability, corroborating the qualitative findings that teachers perceived the solution as useful, easy to integrate and supportive of their practices. … The usability testing of the Escreva Mais was conducted with nine teachers from private and public high schools in Brazil.

summary_evidence_spans: This study aims to systematically evaluate the usability, acceptability and pedagogical relevance of an AIED-Unplugged learning analytics tool from teachers' perspectives, in order to guide the development of user-centered design strategies and support writing practices in resource-constrained educational settings without deepening digital inequities.
We employed a mixed-methods approach involving nine teachers, who downloaded an AIED-U application and followed a predefined usage scenario according to a think-aloud protocol.

Afterwards, participants filled out the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and System Usability Scale (SUS) questionnaires, taking part in a moderated semi-structured interview guided by an interview script.

The quantitative findings indicated high levels of acceptance and usability, corroborating the qualitative findings that teachers perceived the solution as useful, easy to integrate and supportive of their practices.
The usability testing of the Escreva Mais was conducted with nine teachers from private and public high schools in Brazil.
